newsitem.title: USA: Flower company executive gets five years for fraud.
newsitem.headline: Flower company executive gets five years for fraud.

text.p: Former flower magnate George Heublein has been sentenced to five years in prison for cheating investors of tens of millions of dollars in a securities fraud.
U.S. District Judge Helen Frye also sentenced Heublein, 63, to three years for tax fraud, to be served concurrently.

Heublein was captured last year in Florida, where he was working as a grocery bagger, after a nine-year international flight in which he reportedly used eight aliases and bank accounts in Switzerland, Egypt and Panama.
He pleaded guilty to two of 21 tax and fraud charges after his Melridge flower company in Aurora, Ore., went bankrupt.

The company once was reported to be the world's leading hybridizer of lilies, and Heublein bragged it would become the McDonald's of floral suppliers. But he resigned and disappeared in 1987 after directors questioned the company's financial reports.
Investors who lost money have been awarded some $89 million in lawsuits against Melridge and its accountants and lawyers.

U.S. attorney Charles Stuckey said there is still a chance Heublein has money hidden somewhere, but he doesn't have much hope of finding it. Heublein's attorney, Norman Sepenuk, said his client's net worth is less than $2,000.
